# Errors {#sec-errors}

Every C call returns `BIYOS_OK` when it succeeds and a negative error code when it fails. [Error codes](#sec-codes) lists the codes and what each one means.

## Who is at fault {#sec-errors-codes}

The hundreds of a code say who is at fault: −1xx the caller, −2xx the model, −3xx a callback, −4xx resources and −5xx biyos itself.

```{.c file="examples/code/c/errors.c" item="at_fault"}
```

## The last error {#sec-errors-message}

After a failure, `BIYOS_lasterror` reads the status, the model and a message saying what went wrong:

```{.c file="examples/code/c/errors.c" item="report"}
```

```text
-100, at fault the caller, on a model: invalid argument: variable 0: bounds [0, 2] are outside [0, 1], the widest of its kind
-100, at fault the caller, on the environment: invalid argument: option 'seed': -1 is outside [0, 2147483647]
```

Each thread keeps its own last error ([Threads](#sec-threads)).

## What a failure leaves {#sec-errors-state}

A call that fails changes nothing, so the model and the options are as they were before it. The example checks that the refused seed left the option at its default:

```{.c file="examples/code/c/errors.c" item="main"}
```

Every failure is also sent as an event, so a program can log them all in one place ([The events biyos sends](#sec-events-sent)).

## Errors in Python {#sec-errors-python}

A failed call raises `biyos.Error`, which carries the code and the message. Some errors raise a built-in exception instead, before C is called:

| Exception | Raised for |
| --- | --- |
| `TypeError` | a value of the wrong type |
| `ValueError` | an array of the wrong length, or a closed model |
| `OverflowError` | an integer that does not fit in 32 bits |
| `IndexError` | a position outside a block |

```{.python file="examples/code/python/errors.py"}
```
